prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
The Conservative plan is simple: get Brexit done, unite and level up the country, and focus on your priorities with responsible investment, low taxes and strong public services.

My Guarantee if there is a Conservative majority:
- Pass our “oven‑ready” Brexit deal immediately and leave the EU in January.
- Extra NHS funding with 50,000 more nurses, 6,000 more GPs and 50 million more GP appointments a year; 40 new hospitals and 20 upgrades.
- 20,000 more police and tougher sentencing for serious offenders.
- An Australian‑style points‑based immigration system; fast‑track NHS and top science visas.
- Major investment every week in science, schools, skills and infrastructure while controlling debt.
- Net Zero by 2050 through clean energy, innovation and green jobs.
- No rise in the rates of income tax, VAT or National Insurance.

Brexit and the economy:
- Deliver the signed deal, take back control of laws, borders, money and trade; no alignment with EU law; no ECJ. Conclude a UK‑EU FTA in 2020 and will not extend transition.
- Use new freedoms for freeports, global trade deals (USA, Australia, New Zealand, Japan), and services trade; the NHS is not on the table.
- Responsible public finances: invest up to ~3% of GDP in infrastructure; debt falling by end of Parliament.

World‑class public services:
- NHS People Plan: more doctors, nurses, training grants, an NHS Visa, Innovative Medicines Fund, mental health treated with the same urgency as physical health, and free hospital parking for those in greatest need. Clamp down on health tourism; NHS excluded from trade talks.
- Social care: £1bn extra every year, a cross‑party long‑term solution, and no one should have to sell their home to pay for care.
- Schools: £14bn extra over three years, minimum per‑pupil funding, teacher starting pay at £30k, strong discipline, more free schools, arts premium and better SEND support.

Safer streets and justice:
- Empower police (including stop and search), a Police Covenant, new powers against knife crime, 10,000 more prison places, tougher sentences, and a National Crime Laboratory. A Victims’ Law and Domestic Abuse Bill.

Controlled, fair immigration:
- Points‑based system prioritising skills; overall numbers down; equal treatment of EU and non‑EU; five‑year contribution before most benefits; increased NHS surcharge; fix Windrush injustices.

Level up every place:
- A transport and broadband revolution: Northern Powerhouse Rail, Midlands Rail Hub, Beeching reversals, better buses and cycling, EV charging, gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025.
- Towns Fund, Safer Streets Fund, cultural investment, English devolution, and strong local accountability.
- Housing: boost home ownership with long‑term fixed‑rate mortgages, discounts for local/key workers, Right to Buy, renters’ protections (end “no‑fault” evictions), more affordable homes and end rough sleeping.

Backing enterprise, skills and innovation:
- Cut business rates (full review), increase Employment Allowance, pay small firms on time, boost exports, strengthen R&D (to 2.4% of GDP), new high‑risk research agency, and a £3bn National Skills Fund. Fair, tough action on tax avoidance (including a Digital Services Tax).

Environment and rural Britain:
- Environment Bill with a new watchdog; more trees and peatland restoration; cut plastics and boost recycling; no fracking unless proven safe. Support farmers (post‑CAP “public money for public goods”), fishermen (independent coastal state), and rural connectivity.

Strong Union, strong Britain in the world:
- Strengthen the UK’s Union and devolution settlements; oppose a second Scottish referendum; uphold the Belfast Agreement and Northern Ireland’s place in the UK internal market.
- Defence: exceed NATO 2%, modernise forces, maintain Trident, new Space Command, support veterans. Stand up for human rights with Magnitsky sanctions.
- Keep 0.7% aid; lead on girls’ education, media freedom and climate.

The choice: a Conservative majority to get Brexit done, end paralysis and unleash Britain’s potential—or a Corbyn/SNP alliance bringing two referendums, higher taxes, chaos and delay. Vote Conservative to move forward.
